headline: High: Chatwoot’s broad egress plus customer-data handling creates default leakage and compliance risk; prompt-injection and conflict risks are lower because the pair lacks a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is documented for awesome-cli-apps and Chatwoot, so direct injection is not evidenced. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or an undocumented bridge, which the profiles do not show. Because uncertainty must escalate, I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from awesome-cli-apps into Chatwoot without sanitizing it, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or message bridge is added later, attacker-controlled text can cross agents.
mitigations: Use a paste-only workflow with explicit human review.
Strip instructions from copied text before pasting.
Disable any shared clipboard or queue integration.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can leak sensitive support data if Chatwoot content is routed through the other agent or its outputs. The interaction is inferred, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is forwarded to awesome-cli-apps for processing, customer data may leave the support boundary.
IF either agent is given access to the same support transcripts, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep customer transcripts out of awesome-cli-apps.
Redact PII before any cross-agent transfer.
Restrict Chatwoot exports to approved operators.
Audit outbound requests from both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention rules on shared text.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles show broad network egress, but neither documents filesystem write, git mutation, or shared mutable resources. That makes direct capability conflict unproven. The only overlap is network access, which is not enough here to justify medium or higher.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same mutable resource, conflicts become plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared state without locking, race conditions can appear.
mitigations: Avoid giving both agents write access to the same resource.
Separate API credentials per agent.
Review any future shared-state integration.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can act on support workflows and integrations, while awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing/listing agent that could supply unverified text. If Chatwoot treats that output as authoritative, errors can cascade into customer-facing actions. The profiles do not prove this default path, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Chatwoot ingests text from awesome-cli-apps without verification, downstream support actions may be wrong.
IF the output is used to draft replies or update tickets, the cascade becomes customer-visible.
mitigations: Require human review before sending replies.
Mark cross-agent text as untrusted.
Compare outputs against source records.
Limit automation to non-customer-facing drafts.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and messages, while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress and no residency or retention controls are documented. If customer data crosses into the latter, compliance gaps around retention, residency, or logging are plausible. The evidence is indirect, so medium rather than high.
conditions: IF customer data is sent from Chatwoot to awesome-cli-apps, residency and retention controls must be rechecked.
IF logs retain transferred support content, subject-rights handling may be affected.
mitigations: Keep regulated data inside Chatwoot.
Minimize logging on both agents.
Review retention settings before any transfer.
Document data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing controls.
